summary: The lecture covers Indian Railways' history, zones, gauges, and key trains; pipeline and water transport; and Konkan Railway as an engineering marvel. It details the first railway line (1853), 17 railway zones, metro systems, major pipelines, and inland/ocean waterways.
points: First railway line: 1853, Bombay to Thane, 34 km
Indian Railways: largest network in Asia, second largest globally
17 railway zones (Kolkata Metro not counted as separate zone)
First suburban railway: Mumbai, 1925 (local electric trains)
Fastest train: Gatimaan Express (Delhi–Agra), max speed 160 km/h
Vande Bharat Express: semi-high speed, max 180 km/h, operating 120–140 km/h
Meghalaya's first railway station: Mendipathar, opened 2014
Broad gauge width: 1.676 m (1676 mm); meter gauge 1 m; narrow gauge 0.610 m
First metro: Kolkata 1984; 15 cities with metro by 2023; Chennai Metro launched 2015
Konkan Railway: 760 km, Roha (Maharashtra) to Mangalore (Karnataka), 92 tunnels, 2000+ bridges, called engineering marvel
Major pipelines: Assam–Kanpur (crude oil), Salaya–Jalandhar (crude oil), HVJ (Hajira–Vijaipur–Jagdishpur) gas pipeline
Water transport: cheapest for goods; inland waterways (rivers) and ocean waterways (seas)
